harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Recovered both staged print jobs into a persistent CUPS queue named archive. Original payloads remain intact, new raw jobs archive byte-for-byte without physical hardware, and the configuration survived node1’s required reboot.
actions_performed: Installed CentOS Stream 10-compatible CUPS packages without changing the OS release or kernel.
Created an idempotent electronic-archive backend with persistent SELinux labeling.
Recovered J100 and J101 atomically as one file each while retaining their original spool files.
Configured and enabled the raw CUPS queue archive.
Verified live raw submissions before and after reboot.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its changed boot identity and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Recover every staged job exactly once while preserving bytes and original spool files
evidence.summary: J100.prn and J101.prn each have exactly one archived instance, match their source SHA-256 hashes, and both original spool payloads remain present.

evidence.requirement: Provide a working CUPS queue named archive with no physical printer
evidence.summary: CUPS is enabled and active; archive uses the electronic archive URI, accepts requests, and is enabled and idle.

evidence.requirement: New raw jobs follow the same archive path byte-for-byte
evidence.summary: Raw jobs archive-1 and archive-2 completed successfully, producing cups-1.prn and cups-2.prn with hashes identical to their submitted binary payloads, including after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 remained unchanged; CUPS 2.4.10-18.el10 was installed from the platform repositories.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart and recovery evidence
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID be303eb3-eeb6-4466-86f1-fd6406dd7dad was captured, safe reboot acknowledged, disconnect observed, and node1 returned with boot ID a8d8a856-8453-4dff-becc-5c6cf951815c. CUPS, queue state, recovered data, hashes, permissions, SELinux contexts, and a new post-reboot raw job were verified.

attempts.summary: Recovered both staged print jobs into a persistent CUPS queue named archive. Original payloads remain intact, new raw jobs archive byte-for-byte without physical hardware, and the configuration survived node1’s required reboot.
